newsitem.title: UK: EMU delay increasingly likely -- British minister.
newsitem.headline: EMU delay increasingly likely -- British minister.

text.p: A postponement of the planned introduction of a European single currency is looking "increasingly likely", Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang said on Monday.
Interviewed for a BBC financial programme, Lang said: "It's hard to say whether it's absolutely inevitable, but it does look increasingly likely."
Lang said rising unemployment in Germany would inevitably affect the country's budget deficit, a key criterion in deciding whether EU states qualify for monetary union.
"Whether they are able to maintain the three percent of GDP (gross domestic product) target, or whether they will overshoot is a moot point," Lang said.
"In France too there must be some questions. So I would not be at all surprised if the currency were delayed."
Lang's remarks were issued by the BBC in advance of them being broadcast. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
